abstract: A method of damping linearly polarized noise is suggested. This method is applicable for a biorthogonal antenna system when the useful signal has circular polarization. The biorthogonal antenna consists from two systems of orthogonal electrical resonators, which are rotated from each other by 45 degrees. Such a system of electrical resonators has four outputs. The main steps of the suggested method conclude in forming ten difference signals, which are used to check four hypotheses. The choice of the correct hypothesis allows a compensating signal to be formed and the useful signal to be selected from the background noise.

articleTitle: To a problem of the analysis of the dielectric rod radiator
publicationTitle: 4th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques (Cat. No.03EX699)
abstract: A number of problems arising from the analysis and synthesis of dielectric rod antennas is reviewed. Relations of a complex propagation constant and the phase velocity of HE/sub 11/ waves in a dielectric rod from the relation of the rod radius and wavelength are obtained. The field distribution along the rod is analyzed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of an accuracy of determination of amplitude-phase distribution in elements of phased antenna array when measuring dynamic near field amplitude
publicationTitle: 4th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques (Cat. No.03EX699)
abstract: The relationships are indicated for the evaluation of the accuracy of amplitude-phase distribution (APD) determination in elements of a phased antenna array by measurements of the dynamic near field amplitude.

articleTitle: Multi-faced and multibeam DBF antenna for high altitude platforms station stages of antenna development
publicationTitle: 4th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques (Cat. No.03EX699)
abstract: Advantages of the multi-beam antenna for Stratospheric Communication System (or HAPS) with digital beam forming (DBF) are demonstrated in comparison with analogue beam forming (ABF). To cover the service area from nadir to a circle of radius 55 km by 199 beams, the antenna system of seven flat active phased array antennas (APAA) is proposed. Due to high accuracy of amplitudes and phases in channels of the APAA with DBF, optimal cell forming as well as high spatial isolation between cells is obtained. Stages of antenna creating are considered. Results of the work at initial stages are presented too.

articleTitle: The optimization of a signal processing in radar with scanning antenna array
publicationTitle: 4th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques (Cat. No.03EX699)
abstract: It is shown that the scanning radar antenna is an instrument of a selection of echoes from target with intended range and an instrument of a suppression of intensive close clutter. The obtained result is useful to a case of a continuous or quasi-continuous transmitted signal.

articleTitle: 30-element active antenna array as a prototype of a huge low-frequency radio telescope
publicationTitle: 4th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques (Cat. No.03EX699)
abstract: The results of the development of a prototype of a new generation low frequency telescope are discussed. The efficiencies of the new wideband active antenna array and of part of the UTR-2 radio telescope are compared. The radio astronomy observations which have been carried out show the high efficiency of the new active antenna array.

articleTitle: Coaxial collinear antennas with out-of-phase excitation of the elements
publicationTitle: 4th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques (Cat. No.03EX699)
abstract: The paper deals with the capabilities of multielement antennas represented by rigid coaxials "embedded" in one another to form serial coaxial dividers of the antenna feed. Features of such antennas are analyzed by a well-known approximate method. According to this method, patterns are calculated using simplified current distributions represented by circular trigonometric functions. Subsequently, there are determined parameters of equivalent transmission lines with losses. Here, input impedances are estimated by applying a thorough analysis of both the excitation circuit and the radiating structure replaced by equivalent transmission lines. The present paper shows the practicability of such antennas that have out-of-phase excitation of the elements and provide quasioptimal patterns of cosecant shape having a radiation peak at the ground.

articleTitle: Two-element assembly of measuring antennas for a 1-12.75 GHz frequency range
publicationTitle: 4th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques (Cat. No.03EX699)
abstract: The results are considered of the development of a two-element measuring antenna assembly for the range 1-12.75 GHz. It is intended, in particular, for testing the characteristics of anechoic chambers at the indicated range. The assembly consists of two broadband log-periodic antennas with different coefficients of frequency coverage. The main design parameters and electrical characteristics of the antennas are presented.

articleTitle: The robust spatiotemporal filtering of signals in correlated noise
publicationTitle: 4th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques (Cat. No.03EX699)
abstract: A new approach is considered for solving the problem of spatiotemporal signal processing in adaptive antenna arrays working in conditions of intensive correlated noise processes. The method of synthesis of robust algorithms is based on the game-theoretical principle of searching a minimum of the root-mean-square error that characterizes the quality of received estimations of existential spectra. The signal processing algorithms, constructed on this principle, relate to the class of maximal algorithms being invariant with respect to the prior uncertainty concerning noise distribution.

articleTitle: Correction of smart antennas receiving channels characteristics for 4G mobile communications
publicationTitle: 4th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques (Cat. No.03EX699)
abstract: The paper considers a way of correction of the reception channels characteristics for smart-antennas in 4G mobile communications.

articleTitle: The sea wave slope distribution empirical dependencies in calculations of interaction between microwave radiation and rough sea surface
publicationTitle: 4th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques (Cat. No.03EX699)
abstract: The utilization of hydrological (surface wind and sea wave slope) dependencies in radio physical calculations is discussed. An account is given of the results of joint hydrological and radiometric experiments. A quantitative model for microwave (3-50 GHz band) calculations in remote sensing of the "ocean-atmosphere" system is presented.
